item.title: Budapest conference highlights RMB's growing role in trade, financing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Budapest conference highlights RMB's growing role in trade, financing Guests attend a panel discussion during the 10th Budapest Renminbi Initiative Conference in Budapest, Hungary, on Nov. 12, 2026. Themed "The Role of Renminbi in the International Monetary System," the conference was jointly organized by Hungary's central bank and Bank of China CEE Ltd. The annual forum is part of the Budapest Renminbi Initiative, launched by the central bank in 2015 to promote RMB use in Hungary and strengthen financial ties with China. (Xinhua/Hu Zhixuan) BUDAPEST, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- The renminbi (RMB) is broadening financing options for banks and businesses engaged in trade and investment between China and Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), participants said Thursday at the 10th Budapest Renminbi Initiative Conference. Themed "The Role of Renminbi in the International Monetary System," the conference was jointly organized by Hungary's central bank and Bank of China CEE Ltd. The annual forum is part of the Budapest Renminbi Initiative, launched by the central bank in 2015 to promote RMB use in Hungary and strengthen financial ties with China. Hungarian central bank Governor Mihaly Varga said the global financial system was becoming more multipolar, with regional financial networks gaining importance. Cross-border RMB receipts and payments totaled 70.6 trillion yuan (10.57 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 10.1 percent year-on-year, according to the People's Bank of China. "There is no doubt that the RMB will play a very important role in the world economy of the future," Varga said. In an interview with Xinhua, central bank Deputy Governor Daniel Palotai said the initiative aimed to facilitate wider RMB use in financial transactions as more Chinese companies and banks operated in Hungary. "Hungary wants to serve as a bridge between the East and the West in this regard," Palotai said. Chinese battery maker CATL and electric vehicle manufacturer BYD are among the companies investing in Hungary. Chinese companies' planned and implemented investment projects in Hungary were worth more than 26 billion euros (28.8 billion dollars), with over 30,000 jobs created, according to Chinese Ambassador to Hungary Gong Tao. Gong also highlighted financial cooperation projects, including the launch of Central and Eastern Europe's first RMB clearing bank in Hungary in 2015 and Hungary's cumulative issuance of 11 billion yuan (1.65 billion dollars) in sovereign panda bonds. Laszlo Bencsik, deputy CEO and chief strategic and financial officer of Hungary's OTP Bank, said the bank had raised 3.5 billion yuan (525 million dollars) through agreements with major Chinese banks and a dim sum bond issuance over the past few years, helping diversify its funding sources. He said companies earning RMB revenues from exports to China could borrow in the same currency to hedge currency risks. "It has to come as a natural demand from clients," Bencsik said. Yu Wenjian, head of the Shanghai Head Office of the People's Bank of China, said RMB use was expanding beyond trade settlement to financing, investment, pricing and reserves. China would further open its financial markets and improve cross-border payment services, he said. "As Chinese companies go global, the RMB needs to go global too," Wang Huiyao, founder and president of the Center for China and Globalization, told Xinhua, calling for more RMB investment products and accessible financial services for smaller businesses. "International financial cooperation is built over time. It needs consistency and mutual confidence," Palotai said in his closing remarks, expressing hope that the discussions would lead to further cooperation in the years ahead. item.title: APEC Primer in Four Words | Community: What APEC is and how it works
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
APEC Primer in Four Words | Community: What APEC is and how it works This photo shows a flower decoration themed on the 2026 APEC "China Year," in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) APEC Primer in Four Words: The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18 and 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." This four-part series unpacks four key words from that theme, one each day, to explain what APEC is and what the 2026 host year is about. The first of those words is "community," because it answers the most basic question: what kind of group is APEC? Before asking what it means to build a community across a region of vastly different economies, cultures and levels of development, it helps to understand how APEC itself works. A forum, not a treaty APEC was established in 1989 by 12 economies and has since grown to 21. It runs on non-binding commitments, open dialogue and equal respect for the views of all participants. Unlike the World Trade Organization, it places no treaty obligations on its members. Decisions are reached by consensus, and every economy has an equal say. This approach lets economies with different systems, development levels and priorities work together without being bound to commitments they haven't chosen to make. Why "economies" APEC calls its participants "member economies," not "countries." The forum explains that its work centers on trade and economic issues, with members engaging one another as economic entities. The 21 member economies range from Australia, Canada and Chile to Japan, Mexico and Vietnam, and include China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. China joined in 1991. A region of scale Together, APEC's member economies are home to about 36 percent of the world's population. They accounted for more than 61 percent of global real GDP in 2025 and about 46 percent of global trade in goods and commercial services in 2024. The member economies are at very different stages of development, from some of the world's largest economies to much smaller ones. That diversity helps explain why the forum's work has centered on practical goals: reducing barriers to trade and investment, and encouraging economic and technical cooperation. How it works Policy direction comes from the leaders of the 21 economies, backed by recommendations from ministers and senior officials. The APEC Secretariat, based in Singapore, supports the work. The business community also has a voice. The APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) brings together up to three business representatives from each economy to advise officials and leaders, while the annual APEC CEO Summit provides another platform for business engagement. The host role rotates among members each year, and each host proposes a theme and priorities to guide the year's work. China as host China will host the leaders' meeting for the third time in 2026, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year's theme is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," with openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priorities. If APEC is already a community of 21 economies, what does it mean to build one that prospers together? That is the question for the next piece in this series: Prosper. item.title: Explainer: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Explainer: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- In persevering with full and rigorous self-governance, the Communist Party of China (CPC) highlighted efforts to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm in tackling challenges. How will the CPC deliver on this commitment? At the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in October, the CPC leadership sent the signal -- equally important to full and rigorous self-governance is how to encourage Party members and officials to better fulfill their duties, take on new challenges and tackle them. The focus of efforts has been set on creating a clean and enabling political environment. But the drive to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm doesn't stop here. In an enabling political environment, the next thing they need to better serve the people is competence. Currently, the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century, and China is at a critical moment when the foundation for basically realizing socialist modernization needs to be consolidated and all-out efforts should be made to advance the cause. It is more imperative than ever before to improve the competence of officials. Officials need to develop their abilities to advance high-quality development, serve the people, forestall and defuse risks, and apply law-based thinking and approaches in their work. For this purpose, they are encouraged to work at the primary level, keep abreast of new technologies, new industries and new business models, and learn the latest knowledge and expertise required for the fulfillment of duties. The composition of the CPC membership has changed, with officials born after China's reform and opening-up in 1978 taking up an increasingly large share. The healthy career growth of those officials has been highlighted on the agenda of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance. The CPC creates opportunities for them to build up their skills and abilities in practice, whether on the front line of reform, development and stability endeavors, in major tasks, or in challenging but key positions. Targeted training programs revolving around social and economic development goals during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) have been planned to help young officials close the knowledge gap and shore up their weaknesses in fulfilling duties. The CPC also pledged to unequivocally support and speak up for those who assume responsibility and do solid work, particularly when they encounter setbacks or criticisms because of their bold and proactive moves in performing duties, or when they suffer from injustice because of misunderstanding or false accusations. The original aspiration and mission of the CPC are to seek happiness for the Chinese people, and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. The CPC understands that the political ideal of serving the people and good governance cannot be achieved if pursuing power for power's sake or personal benefits becomes the ultimate goal of governance. That's why the CPC has been taking a tough stance against corruption particularly since 2012, and why it places such great importance on building a clean political environment and a contingent of capable officials. Governing the Party with strict discipline, the CPC is protecting the level playing field and stimulating positive energy for shouldering responsibilities. In this sense, such a Party self-governance endeavor bolsters economic and social development, and ultimately the wellbeing of the people. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China-Africa photo exhibition deepens friendship, cultural ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
China-Africa photo exhibition deepens friendship, cultural ties Guests visit the China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, Nov. 12, 2026. China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday here showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. (Xinhua/Geng Xinning) ADDIS ABABA, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. The photographs were captured in more than 30 African countries and China. 24 of them won awards for uniquely depicting the diversity of China and Africa, demonstrating their development, achievements, rich cultural heritage, wildlife and landscapes. Opening the exhibition, Jiang Feng, head of the Chinese Mission to the African Union, said the photography exhibition is a vivid example of China-Africa joint efforts to implement the Global Civilization Initiative that calls for respect for the diversity of civilizations, stronger international people-to-people exchanges, and inclusive coexistence and mutual learning. "The exhibition provides an opportunity to further deepen mutual understanding and friendship between the peoples of China and Africa, enable exchanges among civilizations to transcend barriers, and bring our peoples closer across mountains and seas, thus laying a stronger and more enduring foundation of public support for China-Africa friendship," Jiang said. Noting that the China-Africa friendship has a long history and has grown stronger over time, Jiang hopes that the exhibition will open new opportunities to enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of China and Africa, deepen their cultural exchanges and help build an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future. Mama Keita, deputy executive secretary for programme support at the UNECA, said the photographs showcase everyday moments, bringing together places, cultures and perspectives in a shared visual dialogue, honoring both distinctiveness and common humanity. "I hope these photographs will inspire conversation, broaden our perspectives and encourage us to see our diverse cultures, experiences and heritage with fresh eyes while discovering the common ground that connects China and Africa," she said. The event, co-organized by the Chinese Mission to the African Union and the UNECA, attracted nearly 200 guests. It also came as the two sides celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges. "As we celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, we are reminded that connections between countries are built not only through meetings and agreements, but also through people, curiosity, shared experiences, cultural exchanges and the stories we tell one another," Wubshet Tolosa, representative of award-winning photographers, said during the event. item.title: China's Yangtze River Delta forges new quality productive forces through coordinated development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
China's Yangtze River Delta forges new quality productive forces through coordinated development SHANGHAI, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- In east China's Yangtze River Delta, a four-hour drive can take manufacturers through a network of suppliers capable of providing every component needed to build a new-energy vehicle. At one factory, a six-axis industrial robot can be produced every 12 minutes. These examples reflect a broad shift as the region turns its tightly clustered research and innovation hubs into advanced industrial capacity, making what China calls new quality productive forces the main engine of its growth. The Yangtze River Delta, comprising Shanghai and the provinces of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, now accounts for about one-quarter of China's GDP and nearly one-third of national R&D spending. According to a recent national assessment of regional science and technology innovation, Shanghai ranked first in comprehensive sci-tech innovation nationwide, with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui also among the top performers. INNOVATION CLUSTERS This transformation is particularly visible in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City, where advanced industries are increasingly concentrated. At a lab in the Shanghai R&D center of XtalPi, an AI drug discovery company listed in Hong Kong, human researchers are largely absent. Weighing powders, controlling temperature during mixing, sampling, filtering and running post-processing analyzes are all handled by robotic workstations directed by AI, with large volumes of experimental data flowing continuously to back-end systems. "Zhangjiang offers a unique advantage in clustering innovation resources," said Wang Mingtai, XtalPi's senior vice president. "From overseas partners and major research institutes to upstream and downstream suppliers, connections can be established quickly here." By June 2026, the company had established partnerships with 17 of the world's top 20 pharmaceutical companies. Since the beginning of the year, more than six innovative drug programs involving its discovery technology had reported positive progress in clinical trials. Its autonomous research platform is also being applied in chemicals, new materials and new energy, alongside collaborations with leading universities and research institutes. The expanding network illustrates how Zhangjiang is bringing together scientific research, industrial partners and the development of new medicines and technologies, helping to move discoveries beyond the laboratory. Over the past five years, industrial output from firms above designated size in Zhangjiang has totaled 1.75 trillion yuan (about 260 billion U.S. dollars). In the first half of 2026, its three priority sectors -- integrated circuits, biomedicine and AI -- generated 82.28 billion yuan in output, up 14.8 percent from a year earlier. The area is now home to eight major global chip companies, 35 registered AI large models, and one in ten innovative drugs developed in China. Zhangjiang's experience shows how a concentration of research institutions, technology companies and industrial resources can accelerate innovation, driving new quality productive forces. The same approach is taking shape across the wider Yangtze River Delta, with its four provincial-level divisions complementing one another, especially in AI and the digital economy. COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS A recent digital development report describes this regional division of labor in simple terms: with Shanghai strengthening foundational research, Jiangsu focusing on manufacturing, Zhejiang excelling in application scenarios, and Anhui aggregating computing power. It allows companies to combine capabilities across the region and form a networked innovation system, rather than replicate them in one place. Jiangsu has made "AI Plus" a central driver of manufacturing upgrading. Under its action plan, the penetration rate of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents is expected to exceed 70 percent by 2027, with the AI industry surpassing 1 trillion yuan by 2030. In Suzhou, for example, efforts are underway to develop 150 industrial vertical large models, along with more than 200 high-quality industrial datasets, pushing AI applications from quality control and maintenance deeper into R&D and design. Zhejiang, meanwhile, is encouraging businesses to develop practical applications for AI, activating its intelligent economy. In 2025, the province's core AI industry revenue exceeded 710 billion yuan, growing by more than 20 percent. The capital city, Hangzhou, is positioning itself as a leading "AI city," deploying multimodal large models and embodied intelligence, while a major open-source model community and five 10,000-GPU computing clusters aim to lower the cost for small and medium-sized enterprises to adopt AI. Anhui is focusing on expanding its digital infrastructure and putting it to wider use. The province plans to build 14,000 new 5G base stations and 4,000 5G-A base stations in 2026, with intelligent computing capacity exceeding 65,000 petaflops. A special fund for data-element reform in the province will support AI scenario projects with up to 10 million yuan each, accelerating deployment in manufacturing, public services and healthcare. CROSS-REGIONAL LINKS Cooperation across the Yangtze River Delta extends beyond AI and the digital economy. It also shows how innovation capacity generated in one city can be rapidly converted into industrial output in another. Suzhou, for example, has 50 enterprises in the supply chain for China's C919 passenger aircraft assembled in Shanghai, and about 180 auto-parts manufacturers have become tier-one suppliers for Shanghai-based SAIC Volkswagen and Tesla. Meanwhile, scientific instruments at Shanghai's universities and research institutes can be booked online by Suzhou enterprises for remote testing and cross-regional settlement. As of October 2026, the Yangtze River Delta region had shared 75,000 sets of large-scale scientific instruments, with sci-tech innovation vouchers covering about 820 million yuan in services. These links make integration tangible: firms can access specialized suppliers and costly scientific equipment across administrative boundaries, lowering duplication and making better use of existing resources. Luo Dajin, director of the Shanghai municipal science and technology commission, said Shanghai would build on its strengths as an international economic, financial, trade, shipping and sci-tech innovation hub, and work with Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui to build a sci-tech innovation corridor and other joint innovation zones across the region. Recent data suggest the shift is gaining momentum. In the first three quarters of 2026, high-tech manufacturing output grew 15.1 percent in Jiangsu, 16 percent in Zhejiang and 50.3 percent in Anhui, while Shanghai's three priority industries expanded by 17.1 percent. The region's division of labor has moved beyond the old linear pattern of industrial relocation from Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang to Anhui, and is now shaped by functional and structural complementarity, said Zeng Gang, director of the Institute of Urban Development, East China Normal University. "New quality productive forces have become the main engine of industrial growth in the Yangtze River Delta," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday held positive and constructive phone talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on China-U.S. relations and the interaction between the two heads of state. During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that President Xi Jinping's visit to the United States in September was smooth and successful. The two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-U.S. relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a right approach for the two countries to get along with each other, Wang said. The stable momentum of China-U.S. relations has not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on their respective and common interests, Wang said. China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the U.S. side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results, Wang said. item.title: Beyond China's shopping festival: How Singles' Day shifts from local to global retail barometer
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Beyond China's shopping festival: How Singles' Day shifts from local to global retail barometer A drone photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows an intelligent package sorting line in Xinghua City, east China's Jiangsu Province. (Photo by Zhou Shegen/Xinhua) BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Nearly two decades after its launch, China's Singles' Day shopping festival has become an increasingly influential event in global retail. Overseas brands and e-commerce platforms are adjusting their promotional schedules, supply chains and product launches to tap into the Chinese market. Also known as Double 11 because it falls on Nov. 11, the annual online shopping carnival is one of the world's largest retail events. This year's edition, which has run for nearly a month, is set to conclude, highlighting a shift toward a wider range of services, smarter AI shopping assistants and more vibrant two-way trade through cross-border commerce. SERVICE CONSUMPTION AS A NEW ENGINE During this year's event, major e-commerce platforms expanded their offerings beyond traditional consumer goods and discounts, giving greater prominence to services. JD.com showcased more than 100 service products for the first time, while Suning offered packages such as a 9.9-yuan (about 1.47 U.S. dollars) whole-house appliance inspection. The trend reflects broader changes in China's consumer market, which is now driven by both goods and services. In the first three quarters of this year, service retail sales grew 4 percentage points faster than goods retail sales, making services a key source of incremental consumption. A Beijing resident surnamed Feng said his Double 11 purchases included a two-day hotel package and a home cleaning card. "There are more and more services to choose from. Buying these packages on major platforms offers good value, and fulfillment and after-sales service are more reliable," he said. Physical goods, however, remain a major part of the shopping festival. Sales of smartphones covered by government trade-in subsidies on Tmall surged more than ninefold, while transactions in categories such as maternal and infant products and home appliances on Taobao's on-demand retail platform grew more than 70 percent year on year. Combined sales on China's major integrated e-commerce platforms during the early phase of this year's Singles' Day reached 1.0263 trillion yuan as of Oct. 31, data firm Syntun showed. This year, the Tmall Double 11 event featured 1 million global brands and 72 million products in promotion. That contrasts sharply with the first edition in 2009, when only 27 brands took part and transactions totaled 52 million yuan. AI ELEMENTS One notable development this year was the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) tokens as an independent product category on multiple e-commerce platforms, a sign that AI is rapidly integrating into every link of the e-commerce chain. Taobao, Douyin and Pinduoduo all embedded smarter AI shopping functions during this year's Double 11. Last year, Taobao and JD.com introduced AI shopping guides that could answer product questions and search by photo. This year, many platforms rolled out conversational AI shopping assistants for the first time -- tools that can sort shopping carts, automatically calculate combined discounts and subsidies, and handle after-sales follow-up. Li Mingtao, chief e-commerce expert at the China International Electronic Commerce Center, said consumers' use of AI shopping assistants has moved from trial to large-scale adoption, and the expanding functions mark a shift from tools to intelligent agents. "In previous years, consumers spent considerable time hunting for coupons and comparing prices. AI shopping assistants take on that time burden, turning complex promotional rules into clear, actionable shopping plans," Li said. AI is also changing how online retailers operate, improving efficiency and streamlining operations. Alibaba's QwenWork launched an e-commerce version ahead of Singles' Day, while JD.com upgraded its AI business center to provide merchants with dozens of tools covering product selection, operations, fulfillment and after-sales. GLOBAL RESONANCE The festival's influence is increasingly extending beyond China. With the rise of global digital consumption and improving cross-border e-commerce policies, many platforms and merchants looked overseas for new growth during this year's event, while international brands are leveraging China's Singles' Day to expand market share. This year, Taobao opened a one-click overseas channel for the first time, allowing merchants to sell in both domestic and overseas markets with their existing stores and products. AliExpress's official warehouses covered six countries, with pre-event overseas warehouse inventory up 146 percent year on year. "Going overseas is not simply about selling goods abroad," said Sun Yanyan, head of Sparkone Media, a cross-border e-commerce company. "It is about exporting China's mature digital retail, supply chain and AI operations capabilities, building a two-way channel that helps transform Chinese manufacturing into Chinese brands and better connects domestic and international markets." While platforms expand overseas, quality imported goods continue to enrich choices for Chinese consumers. A Shanghai resident surnamed Liu bought Australian infant food and Belgian nutritional supplements on Tmall Global during Singles' Day. "In the past, many overseas local brands were hard to buy," she said. "Now the platform has sufficient bonded warehouse stock and fast customs clearance and delivery, so I can shop for specialty goods from around the world without traveling abroad." Currently, imported food products on the Taobao and Tmall platforms cover more than 100 countries, over 1,000 production regions, and more than one million items. This year, the Singles' Day festival coincided with the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10. The expo attracted 4,142 overseas companies from 162 countries, regions and international organizations, with more than 480 representative new products making their debuts. Many of these products were not merely on display -- they were simultaneously listed on Singles' Day platforms, shortening the distance between global innovation and Chinese consumers. At the Tmall Global booth, AI-related gadgets were among the highlights: Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, Oura smart rings and Fitbit Air wristbands were launched simultaneously at the CIIE and on Singles' Day. According to Tmall Global, more than 1,800 new brands opened stores on the platform over the past year, and 1,300-plus imported brands participated in Singles' Day for the first time. To address information gaps in cross-border shopping, Tmall Global launched a "Global Traceability Program" in May this year. More than 50 global brands have joined, and more than half of participating brands recorded double-digit year-on-year sales growth during this year's Singles' Day. Besides Taobao and Tmall, other Chinese platforms such as Temu, Shein and TikTok Shop have brought Double 11 promotions to dozens of countries, while some Western retailers have adjusted their year-end promotional calendars in response. Eighteen years on, Singles' Day no longer belongs to one country or one platform. From promotional calendars and logistics to product categories and consumer trust, it has become a global retail landmark -- and for many, an increasingly important indicator of changes in China's consumer market and of how the country continues to innovate and open up. item.title: Sharing the benefits of openness to promote common prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Sharing the benefits of openness to promote common prosperity Visitors view an exhibit at the Cadillac booth at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Han Shuo) As a major engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region is characterized by deep economic integration and closely interconnected industrial sectors. Through business matchmaking and industrial cooperation, the China International Import Expo (CIIE) has provided a broad platform for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies to share opportunities and promote development, contributing to deeper and more substantive progress in building an Asia-Pacific community. The ninth CIIE, held in east China's Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10, coincided with the 2026 APEC China Year. Exhibits from APEC economies traveled far and wide to the expo, where displays, discussions, and business matchmaking turned exhibition booths into starting points for cooperation and products into bridges to new markets. U.S. exhibitors secured more than 50,000 square meters of exhibition space, the largest area among participating economies for the eighth consecutive year, up 1,500 square meters from the previous year. A robot performs a picking task at the booth of a South Korean company at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Cao Pengcheng) Canadian and New Zealand exhibitors recorded their largest exhibition areas to date, while Australian exhibitors expanded their space by 25 percent year on year. These figures reflect strong participation by APEC economies, with both exhibition scale and product diversity continuing to grow. Marriott International, which has participated in the CIIE for nine consecutive years, has witnessed the continued expansion of China's consumer services market. Mao Yibing, a member of Marriott International's global executive committee and president of the company's China operations, said China's continued efforts to promote high-standard opening-up, its thriving tourism market, and evolving consumer demand have created broad opportunities for international hotel groups. In 2021, New Zealand-based Pacific Alpacas brought more than 100 alpaca duvets to the CIIE. The products quickly sold out at its 9-square-meter booth. A year later, the company shipped 3.3 metric tonnes of New Zealand alpaca fiber to China and partnered with Chinese companies to process the material using China's advanced fiber-combing techniques. In 2025, it established long-term partnerships with Chinese e-commerce platforms. Hu Tao, chairman of Pacific Alpacas, said the CIIE provided the company with not only access to a vast market but also opportunities to work with various partners to improve its products and upgrade its industrial and value chains. A visitor learns about specialty products from a Malaysian exhibitor at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in east China's Shanghai. (People's Daily/Li Anqi) For many small and medium-sized enterprises from APEC economies, the CIIE has opened up valuable opportunities to expand their markets and reach global consumers. Australian Natural Biotechnology Pty. Ltd (ANB) has participated in every edition of the expo, with its main product, Karibee Eucalyptus Pure Honey, continuing to gain popularity in the Chinese market. Alpaca wool toys from Peru have also used the CIIE as a springboard into China, with orders generated at the expo helping more than 200 local artisan families improve their livelihoods. APEC helps economies across the Asia-Pacific build consensus through dialogue and consultation and promote free trade and open cooperation, while the CIIE provides an important platform for translating these shared goals into tangible outcomes, said Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, president of the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia. The expo not only facilitates access to the Chinese market for products from participating economies, but also strengthens trade ties among APEC members, he noted. This year's CIIE focused on cutting-edge industries and innovation, showcasing new technologies, products, and services from participating economies and helping APEC economies tap into opportunities arising from China's high-quality development through innovative offerings. During the expo, many visitors tried out Singaporean company OSIM's flagship massage chair, which made its China debut at the event, at Hall 5 of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the expo. Deserine Lim, general manager of headquarters management at OSIM China, said the CIIE served as a launchpad for cutting-edge technologies from around the world to enter the Chinese market and as an important hub connecting China's innovation needs with markets across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond. She added that the expo had enabled the company to create a virtuous cycle of "rooted in China, empowering the Asia-Pacific," allowing innovative products that integrate global technologies with local Chinese needs to benefit consumers across the Asia-Pacific region more effectively and quickly. The development of the Asia-Pacific region has shown that openness and cooperation create mutual benefits. This year's CIIE brought together leading companies from across regional industrial chains, fostering partnerships to strengthen the stability of regional industrial and supply chains. The Canada International Trade Promotion Society (CITPS) has brought Canadian companies to the expo for nine consecutive years. Jeannie Cheng, president of the CITPS, said the CIIE serves as a trade and economic bridge connecting businesses and markets, and that behind a product's journey into Chinese households lies a cooperation network spanning multiple APEC economies. She cited Canadian seafood and fresh fruit as examples, explaining that Canadian companies handle production and quality control, while Chinese partners are responsible for imports, distribution, and sales and economies such as Singapore and South Korea provide financial, logistics and testing services. By leveraging their respective strengths at different stages, economies across the region are strengthening economic ties and deepening cooperation, she said. Zhang Daijun, executive vice president of Samsung China, said the CIIE offers a vivid illustration of China's commitment to expanding high-standard opening-up, and that the expo is underpinned by China's vast domestic market, well-developed industrial chain support system, and vibrant innovation ecosystem. China has become a global manufacturing hub, a major center for research and development, and a key hub in global supply chains, he said. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is scheduled to take place in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, from November 18 to 19. Business negotiations, technology launches, and investment projects at the CIIE have offered concrete examples of Asia-Pacific cooperation. Under the summit's theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the shared vision of openness, innovation, and cooperation is being translated into practical action across the region, injecting fresh momentum into common development.
